topics.title: OrcaSlicer 2.5.0 Alpha: Plugins, Color Mixing and a CAD Tab
topics.description: "The most feature-packed release in OrcaSlicer's history": 950 pull requests from 140 contributors, out October 16

slides.heading: OrcaSlicer 2.5.0 Alpha: Plugins, Color Mixing and a CAD Tab
slides.body: Released October 16 as an alpha: more than 950 pull requests from over 140 contributors.
bullets: Python plugins: add features without forking the slicer. A plugin must ask before it touches your files, goes online, or launches programs
Speed Dial: press Space and type the command or setting you want
Color mixing: blend two or three loaded filaments into new colors. "Decompose Color" works out the mix for a target shade
Texture Displacement: paint a region, pick one of 40+ textures or your own image, bake a printable relief

slides.heading: Also New, and the Alpha Caveat
bullets: Belt printers, and parallel printing on IDEX and IQEX machines: two to four parts at once
Profiles for the Bambu H2C and A2L, mixed nozzle sizes on the H2D and X2D
An experimental Design tab: sketch-based parametric CAD inside the slicer, off by default
Faster startup, slicing and G-code export
It's an alpha. Back up your profiles and projects before you try it. 2.4.2 from July is still the stable release

topics.title: OpenCAL V2: Build Your Own Layerless Resin Printer for $1,600
topics.description: UC Berkeley, Prusa and Formlabs release an open-source volumetric printer. The whole part forms at once inside a spinning vial

slides.heading: OpenCAL V2: Build Your Own Layerless Resin Printer
slides.body: Released October 20 by UC Berkeley with Prusa Research and Formlabs. Computed axial lithography: a projector shines patterns into a spinning vial of resin and the whole part solidifies at once.
bullets: No layers, no supports. A Rodin's Thinker replica in 90 seconds; inch-scale parts in one to two minutes
About $1,600 in parts and about six hours to assemble: a consumer LED projector, a Raspberry Pi 5, a stepper, extrusion, acrylic and printed parts
Already running at MIT, NIST and Purdue

slides.heading: Everything Is Public, Including the Resin Recipe
bullets: Hardware under Prusa's Open Community License. Printable parts on Printables, code on GitHub, docs on Read the Docs
Formlabs makes the OpenCAL resin and Prusa sells it through Printed Solid: $119.99 per liter. The formula is published too
The free Tomo app turns an STL into the projection sequence
Resin printing without a vat, a film or a support strategy. Worth watching for the kit someone will sell

topics.title: The Sub-Minute Benchy Guy Pushes Six Meters of Filament a Minute
topics.description: Roetz 4.0, October 17: the cable-driven Minute Man after a 59-second Benchy, now chasing five meters per second

slides.heading: I Broke the 3D-Printing Speed Limit
slides.body: Roetz 4.0, October 17. The follow-up to his 59-second Benchy: new extruder, new steppers, and a run at the real limits of the hot end.

slides.heading: The Numbers
bullets: The Minute Man: a cable-driven printer bolted to a 1,300 kg coordinate measuring machine. Moving mass about 60 grams
September: a 59-second Benchy at 1,700 mm/s and 200 g of acceleration, with most of the print near 200 mm³/s
This video: about six meters of filament a minute, roughly 240 mm³/s, and head speeds of four to five meters per second
Four Bondtech extruders feed one melt chamber. The hot end tops out near 400 mm³/s
What breaks next: stepper comms over USB and keeping the plastic cool enough to stack

topics.title: Compliant Gears: Springy Teeth, No Backlash
topics.description: Seve's hollow-tooth gears preload themselves against the mating gear. OpenSCAD files are on GitHub under MIT

slides.heading: Compliant Gears: Springy Teeth, No Backlash
slides.body: Seve, October 5. 184,000 views. Hollow teeth with two thin flank walls that flex, so the pair runs with no play.

slides.heading: How It Works, and the Files
bullets: Each tooth is cut 0.10 mm oversize per flank. At the normal center distance the mating gear pushes the walls in, which takes up the play
The rack-and-pinion version (October 15) does the same trick on a linear rail
Parametric OpenSCAD on GitHub, MIT. STL, STEP and the source. Version 2 has 45-degree caps, so it prints without supports
No load or wear numbers yet. Great for positioning, probably not for torque

topics.title: Creality: K3 Ships November 2, and a 420 mm Ender-3 for $669
topics.description: The K3 pre-order page now has a ship date. The Ender-3 V3 Mega Combo is a 420 mm cube with a four-color unit

slides.heading: Creality: K3 Ships November 2, and a 420 mm Ender-3 for $669
bullets: K3: $849 pre-order, estimated shipping November 2. Four free rolls through November 30. Still no independent review
Ender-3 V3 Mega: 420 × 420 × 420 mm bed-slinger, up to 500 mm/s, new Sprite-2 extruder rated for 85A to 95A TPU
Mega Combo with the CFS Nano four-color unit: $669 early bird through November 10. The Ender-3 V3 Neo Combo is $329
Announced October 15. All Creality's own numbers, no reviews yet

topics.title: Scanners: Creality's $699 Pika Reviewed, Bambu's S1 Still a Tease
topics.description: Tom's Hardware reviews the Pika handheld scanner. Bambu's first scanner is coming in November with no specs or price

slides.heading: Scanners: Creality's $699 Pika Reviewed, Bambu's S1 Still a Tease
bullets: Tom's Hardware, October 19: the Pika is 260 grams with batteries. A blue-laser mode that needs marker dots, and an infrared mode that doesn't
Cordless with a recent phone. On a laptop you want 16 GB of RAM; 8 GB failed
Weak spots: hair and tracking in infrared mode, play in the turntable bearing. Creality's Sermoon scanners start at $2,069
Bambu S1: teased October 12, page says November. An FCC filing shows 60 W and 5 GHz Wi-Fi. Every price you've seen is a guess

topics.title: A Year in the Ground: PLA Does Not Compost
topics.description: Hackaday, October 16: buried PLA samples came back unchanged after a full year in soil and compost

slides.heading: A Year in the Ground: PLA Does Not Compost
slides.body: Hackaday, October 16: the "I built a thing" experiment buried PLA in soil and in compost for a full year, next to a control set.
bullets: Dug up: no visible change, no statistically significant change in tensile strength
Microcalorimetry at the University of Basel: soil microbes don't feed on PLA
Industrial composters in Switzerland, Germany and the US take PLA in principle. None would accept printed parts; too slow to pay
Alternatives named: PHA, which breaks down without the hydrolysis step, or PETG for parts that should last
So what do we do with the scrap bin?

topics.title: Your Favorite Last Week: The Vibe-Coding Era
topics.description: Two hearts for the vibe-coding era. The list grew again this week, and the biggest entry is a CAD skill for your AI agent

slides.heading: Last Week's Hearts: The Vibe-Coding Era
slides.body: Four hearts last week; the vibe-coding era took two. The list, one week later:
bullets: SolidCraft: a free take on Fusion. JumpStart 3D: between Fusion and Tinkercad. Layerling: a Tinkercad you host yourself
New: text-to-cad, a skill that gives Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or Gemini a CAD kernel. STEP, STL and 3MF out. 22,000 stars
Fair warning: text-to-cad sends usage stats by default. One command turns it off
Tap the heart on any topic in the archive. It tells me what to cover more of

topics.title: Robotics Corner: RoboParty RP1, a Fully Open-Source Humanoid
topics.description: Every drawing, board and BOM of a 1.35 m humanoid is public. Plus the SO-ARM102, a $439 printable arm kit

slides.heading: Robotics Corner: RoboParty RP1
slides.body: RoboParty's launch video, October 14. The formal launch followed on October 15 after a debut at IROS, where they kicked it and it stayed up.

slides.heading: What's Actually Open
bullets: 1.35 m, about 39 kg, 24 active degrees of freedom; the Pro has 30 with a neck and seven-joint arms. Their own joint modules peak at 160 N·m
10 Ah hot-swap battery: three hours of runtime, 90 minutes to charge
The hardware repo has the SolidWorks sources, drawings, Gerbers, harnesses and a BOM spreadsheet. The software side is ROS 2, Isaac Lab training and firmware
Honest caveat: you can't print this one. The body is CNC aluminum and engineering plastic. No price, no ship date yet
Their first robot, Roboto Origin, was the DIY one: 2,700 stars since January

slides.heading: SO-ARM102: The SO-101 Grows Up, $439 for Two
bullets: Robonine's successor to the SO-101 LeRobot arm. Leader plus follower kit, $439, first batch ships late October, you assemble it
Parallel gripper to 85 mm instead of one angular jaw. Payload 300 g, up from 150. Reach 483 mm. Tip deflection halved
PET-CF frame instead of PLA, about 90% of the parts printed. STEP, STL, BOM and the print guide are on GitHub
Same joint layout as the SO-101, so your LeRobot datasets still work. The LeRobot plugin is an alpha from October 17

topics.title: Builder Spotlight: JumpStart 3D, One Week Later
topics.description: The author came back with version 2.0 under MIT, and the community fork shipped 20 releases in six days

slides.heading: Builder Spotlight: JumpStart 3D, One Week Later
slides.body: Last week I said I was hosting JumpStart 3D and didn't know who wrote it. This week I do: J.Siwek is back, with version 2.0 and the full source under MIT.
bullets: Free CAD in your browser. No install, no account, no server. Beginner mode drags shapes; Advanced mode sketches, extrudes, fillets and shells on a real CAD kernel
His 2.0 added 3D Sketch, a Lathe, Jump Brick Builder, patterns along a path, and a 256 mm build plate
Our fork tracks his releases and adds its own work under the same license. 124 stars and 43 forks in a week

slides.heading: What Shipped This Week: 20 Releases in Six Days
bullets: An AI chat inside the app: pick a model, type "a 40 by 30 by 20 block with an 8 mm hole," watch it build. Ollama, LM Studio, OpenAI-style or Anthropic
An MCP server, so Claude Code or Codex can edit the design you have open and export STL, STEP, OBJ or 3MF
Fastener, Gear, Hole-pattern and Name-plate dialogs: real threads with a print offset, involute gears with clearance, counterbored rows of holes
Named parameters everywhere, and patterns you can edit later
Back up and restore every design, save copies to a folder, or keep them on your own server over WebDAV

slides.heading: Try It, Break It, Tell Me
bullets: Online: maxsikorski.github.io/jumpstart-3d. Offline: download one HTML file and double-click it
Claude Code users: two commands install the plugin. The README has the lines for Codex, Cursor and Gemini CLI
The subreddit is new and public: r/Jumpstart3D. Bug reports, feature asks and your designs go there
Built with AI, now shipping an AI. This is what the vibe-coding era looks like from the inside

topics.title: Quick Tip of the Week
topics.description: Model small tabs onto your part's corners instead of adding mouse ears in the slicer

slides.heading: Quick Tip: Tabs Instead of Mouse Ears
slides.body: Contrive Design Innovations, October 8. One minute: a design trick against warping you add in CAD, not in the slicer.

slides.heading: How It Works
bullets: Model thin tabs on the corners and long edges of the part, one layer or two thick, as part of the model
They print with the first layer, hold the corners down, and snap or trim off when the part is done
Unlike mouse ears, they travel with the model file, so every print of it gets them
Works on anything with sharp corners in ABS, ASA or big flat PLA
